examples.title: Direct Mode Calculator
examples.description: Type a sum without a line number and the C64 works it out at once.

examples.title: Hello World
examples.description: The traditional first program: one PRINT and the C64 says hello.

examples.title: Count to 10
examples.description: A FOR...NEXT loop counts from 1 to 10, one number per line.

examples.title: Dice Roller
examples.description: Rolls a six-sided die with RND every time you press a key.

examples.title: Name Input
examples.description: Asks for your name with INPUT and greets you, again and again.

examples.title: Infinite Loop
examples.description: Two lines that never stop. Press RUN/STOP (Esc) to break in.

examples.title: Border Flasher
examples.description: Pokes the border colour register at 53280 as fast as BASIC can go, so the border flickers rapidly.

examples.title: Maze One-liner
examples.description: The famous one-liner: random diagonal characters build an endless maze.

examples.title: Balloon Sprite
examples.description: Builds a balloon sprite from DATA and floats it across the screen.

examples.title: Bouncing Ball
examples.description: A ball bounces off the edges, drawn straight into screen and colour memory.

examples.title: The 16 Colours
examples.description: Every colour the C64 can show, with its number and its name.

examples.title: Twinkling Stars
examples.description: Stars twinkle in random colours, poked straight into screen memory.

examples.title: SID Beep
examples.description: One note on SID voice 1: set the volume, envelope and pitch, then open the gate.

examples.title: Ascending Scale
examples.description: A sawtooth wave climbs in pitch as the frequency register counts up.

examples.title: Ode to Joy
examples.description: Beethoven on the SID chip, played from frequencies in DATA lines.

examples.title: Guess the Number
examples.description: Find the secret number between 1 and 100. Peek at N in the program view to cheat!

examples.title: Reaction Test
examples.description: Press a key when the border turns red, and the TI clock times you.

examples.title: Times Tables
examples.description: Pick a number and a FOR...NEXT loop prints its times table.

examples.title: Joystick Tester
examples.description: Reads both joystick ports from the CIA chip and lights up each direction.
